title: Control Scrapbook — encryption & evidence ideas
content:
Scrapbook / rough thinking (not for distribution)

Goal: collect minimal reproducible evidence for encryption, key mgmt, and logging controls for Private + Dedicated customers. Keep this lightweight — want artifacts we can point auditors at without heavy engineering cycles.

High-level mapping ideas (control -> artifact types):
- Key management (KMS/HSM) / C3 equivalent: KMS console screenshots, KMS policy JSON, rotation schedule (cron + ops-runbook), comments on HSM attestation if used.
- Encryption in transit: load balancer TLS config exports, cert expiry checks, automated health check logs showing TLS handshake OK, CA chain names.
- Encryption at rest: disk encryption flags (cloud provider), image build notes showing dm-crypt/LUKS usage for on-prem images, storage class encryption metadata.
- Access controls / IAM: IAM role definitions (minimal set), last-used report for service principals, sample AWS/GCP audit event for a denied call, RBAC bindings in k8s for private cluster.
- Logging & retention: sample log export (one-day slice), retention policy file from logging stack, sample query showing deleted-user events.
- Change control / deployments: CI pipeline run artifact (build + deploy), PR->merge->deploy timeline for a config change (with tags).

Quick checklist (next actions):
- [ ] Draft short template email for eng owners requesting last 12 months of key rotation logs and KMS policy export. Keep the ask specific: path, timeframe, who performed operation, and why.
- [ ] Write 1-liner description for each artifact to include in audit packet (what it proves, how it was generated).
- [ ] Create tiny script to pull KMS policy + key metadata and output human-readable summary (haruki/priority).
- [ ] Capture and redact 3 console screenshots: KMS key details, IAM role trust policy, storage encryption settings.
- [ ] Confirm where private-deploy audit logs live (VPC flow vs. app logs) and add path.

Open questions / risks to resolve:
- How to demonstrate customer data separation for Dedicated capacity? We have tenancy docs but need a concrete example of resource tagging + network policy enforcement. Possible artifact: network ACL dump + a single tenant traffic flow trace.
- On-prem images: do we record attestation or just build-time signed manifest? If HSM signing is available, that’s better — check with release-eng.
- Do we have a single source-of-truth for retention policy? Console shows retention override sometimes; need to validate infra as-code value (terraform).

Minimal evidence templates (short):
- KMS policy export: include who can manage, who can use; include a sample CLI command used to pull it (aws kms get-key-policy --key-id X --policy-name default).
- Rotation log snippet: timestamp, principal, operation (RotateKey), keyId, requestId. Prefer a 3-line excerpt and a script that extracts timewindow.
- IAM last-used: pasted CSV export with header row + a short note on how to interpret last_used_date.

Proposed short lifecycle for a control artifact request (to move from this scratchpad -> final packet):
1) Fill in artifact template (owner, reason, generation command, sample excerpt).
2) Owner runs script/command and places artifact in secure evidence bucket (e.g., s3://redwood-evidence/<eng-team>/).
3) Trust-ops verifies artifact, adds redaction if needed, records metadata in confluence evidence table.
4) Keep a signed checksum + timestamp in the table (sha256).

Notes for Private deployment specifics (product tie-ins):
- Customers on Private can manage KMS themselves (customer KMS) or use Redwood-managed KMS. Evidence should clearly show which mode is used. When customer-managed: we need a documented handshake (key ID + proof of use) rather than Redwood-held credentials.
- For dedicated GPU pools, ensure we can show node disk encryption flag + image fingerprint (AMI hash or image signature).
- For VPC logs: pick 7-14 days of flow logs to show deny/allow decisions for a manifest example; redact IPs.

People to ping:
- Lina (ask for last rotation logs, she maintains key ops)
- Haruki (can prototype KMS-export script)
- Release-eng lead (image signing / attestations)
- Solutions eng (customer-specific evidence examples)

Slack threads / tickets to attach: SEC-482 (kms permissions follow-up), infra-slack thread "kms-rotation-2026" (link in confluence).

Mini brain-dump — language to use in packet (short):
"This artifact demonstrates that encryption keys used for production are subject to documented lifecycle management: creation, role-based administration, automated rotation, and audit logging. The attached logs and policy exports enable verification without exposing sensitive key material."

Fragment TODOs / future expansions:
- Consider small internal demo video (1-2 minutes) showing admin performing rotation in staging, capturing console, CLI, and resulting audit event.
- Automate monthly snapshot of evidence bucket into an immutable store (time-based retention + checksum).
- Build a one-command collector for Trust-ops that asks for timeframe and outputs zipped, redacted packet.

Random thoughts: keep artifacts minimal and machine-verifiable where possible. Auditors like reproducible steps. But don’t leak secret values — prefer metadata and event confirmation rather than key material.

Endnotes: save this file as scratch only. Move finalized templates into confluence once we have 3-4 completed controls with owner and sample artifacts.

-- Eden
